title: A Change of Heart
cn: 第 18 集 · 心的改变
novel: Barney started to worry that something was wrong with his heart. He had been developing real feelings for Nora, and the [[sensation|sensation]] was completely [[foreign|foreign]] to him. He felt his heart [[race|races]] every time he saw her, and he could not eat or sleep properly. He went to see a doctor, who told him that there was nothing [[physically|physical]] wrong with his heart. The problem was [[emotional|emotional]]. Barney was experiencing genuine love for the first time in his life, and it [[terrified|terrify]] him. Meanwhile, Robin started dating a man named Nate who behaved like a dog. He [[chased|chase]] balls, barked at strangers, and ate food off the floor. Robin found it [[bizarre|bizarre]] but also oddly endearing. Her friends thought she had lost her mind. Barney decided to [[confess|confess]] his feelings to Nora on a national television show. It was a [[grand|grand]] gesture that surprised everyone, including Barney himself. Nora was [[touched|touch]] by his honesty but was not sure if she could trust him. She told Barney that she needed time to think. While Barney waited for Nora's answer, he reflected on his life. He realized that every woman he had ever been with had been a [[substitute|substitute]] for the real connection he was afraid to seek. Robin broke up with Nate after he bit the mailman. She told the gang that she had been dating him only to distract herself from her feelings for Barney. Ted listened to Robin's [[confession|confession]] and felt [[concerned|concern]] for both of his friends. He knew that the situation was [[delicate|delicate]] and that someone was going to get hurt. Eventually, Nora agreed to give Barney a chance. Barney was so [[overjoyed|overjoyed]] that he literally danced in the street. He felt like a new man, as if his heart had undergone a complete [[transformation|transformation]]. It was a true change of heart in every sense of the word.

foreign.en: not familiar or not from your own country

races.en: to beat very fast, like a heart from fear

physical.en: relating to the body rather than the mind

terrify.en: to make someone feel extremely afraid

chase.en: to run after someone or something

confess.en: to admit something you have been hiding

substitute.en: a thing that takes the place of another

confession.en: the act of admitting something hidden

delicate.en: needing careful handling to avoid problems

transformation.en: a complete change in appearance or nature
